Sat Nov 7film-tv

'Godzilla Minus Zero' opens to an estimated $31 million, topping the weekend

Toho and GKids' "Godzilla Minus Zero" is on course for an estimated $31 million opening weekend after taking in about $14.5 million to $14.7 million on Friday from 3,254 North American theaters, Variety and TheWrap reported.

Fri Nov 6business

Fox completes $22 billion acquisition of Roku, keeps platform as open streaming ecosystem

Fox Corporation said Friday it closed its roughly $22 billion acquisition of streaming platform Roku, creating Fox Digital Platforms with Roku, Tubi and Fox One, while pledging to keep Roku an open ecosystem for other services, Fox, Variety and The Verge reported.

Fri Nov 6film-tv

Godzilla Minus Zero roars to $6.7 million in North American previews

Toho and GKids' Godzilla Minus Zero took in about $6.7 million in North American previews by Friday and was tracking toward roughly a $30 million opening, more than double the debut of 2023's Godzilla Minus One, Variety and Deadline reported.

Fri Nov 6earnings

Lionsgate quarterly revenue jumps 41% on Michael and TV deliveries

Lionsgate Studios reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $668.8 million, up 41% year over year, and narrowed its net loss from continuing operations to $15.5 million, aided by the Michael biopic and higher scripted TV deliveries, the company, Variety and Deadline said.

Fri Nov 6music

Sony music segment posts double-digit growth; full-year forecast raised

Sony's music segment reported about 598 billion yen in quarterly revenue and about 123 billion yen in operating income for the three months ended September 2026, and raised its full-year music sales forecast to 2.30 trillion yen, Billboard and Music Business Worldwide reported from Sony results.

Thu Nov 5earnings

IMAX posts record Q3 revenue of $175 million as The Odyssey tops $550 million on IMAX screens

IMAX reported Thursday that third-quarter revenue rose 64% to $174.6 million and net income jumped to $117.1 million, powered by Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, the company said.

Thu Nov 5film-tv

Universal will re-release Nolan's The Odyssey on more than 1,000 screens starting Dec. 11

Universal Pictures said Thursday that Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey will return to more than 1,000 screens in the U.S. and Canada, including IMAX and IMAX 70mm, beginning Dec. 11, after a home release on Nov. 17.

Thu Nov 5music

Influence Media completes $600 million-plus purchase of Anthem Entertainment catalogs

Influence Media Partners said Thursday it has completed its acquisition of substantially all of Anthem Entertainment's assets in a transaction valued at over $600 million, in collaboration with funds and accounts managed by BlackRock affiliates.

Wed Nov 4regulation

UK culture secretary orders public-interest review of Sky's planned ITV acquisition

U.K. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy on Wednesday issued a public interest intervention notice on Sky's proposed purchase of ITV's broadcasting and streaming business, requiring the Competition and Markets Authority and Ofcom to report on the deal, the U.K. government and Variety said.

Wed Nov 4music

Suno asks court to dismiss Jason Isbell's lawsuit over artist names in AI music prompts

AI music company Suno on Tuesday asked a federal court in Massachusetts to dismiss a proposed class action by Jason Isbell and other musicians, arguing that letting users name artists to describe a musical style is lawful, Variety and Music Business Worldwide reported.

Wed Nov 4earnings

TKO raises its full-year outlook again as UFC revenue jumps 60% in the third quarter

TKO Group Holdings, owner of UFC, WWE and IMG, reported Wednesday that third-quarter revenue rose 21% to $1.36 billion and raised its full-year guidance for the second time this year, the company said.

Mon Nov 2policy

Newsom proposes raising California's film and TV tax credit to at least $1 billion a year

California Gov. Gavin Newsom on Monday proposed expanding the state's film and television tax credit program from $750 million a year to at least $1 billion, Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter reported.

Mon Nov 2entertainment

Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell named 2026 Kennedy Center honorees

The Kennedy Center on Monday named singer-songwriter Paul Anka, composer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia, playwright David Mamet and country singer Barbara Mandrell as this year's Kennedy Center Honors recipients, Variety and Deadline reported.

Mon Nov 2earnings

Roku's third-quarter revenue rises 24% to $1.5 billion as its Fox merger awaits U.S. review

Roku reported Monday that third-quarter revenue rose 24% from a year earlier to $1.5 billion and net income reached $183 million, or $1.20 a share, The Hollywood Reporter and Deadline reported.

Mon Nov 2film-tv

Lionsgate and Meta convert new 'Hunger Games' film to 3D, with a later release on Meta's VR glasses

Lionsgate said Monday that Meta helped convert "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" to 3D for its Nov. 20 theatrical release, the first time Meta has worked with a studio on such a conversion, and that the 3D version will later play on Meta's VR glasses, Variety and Deadline reported.

Mon Nov 2film-tv

Netflix acquires Joel Coen's 'Jack of Spades' for a fall 2027 theatrical release

Netflix has acquired worldwide rights to Joel Coen's gothic mystery "Jack of Spades," starring Patsy Ferran, Josh O'Connor, Damian Lewis and Lesley Manville, and plans a theatrical release in fall 2027 before it streams, Variety and Deadline reported Monday.

Sun Nov 1film-tv

'You Can See Everything' tops slow Halloween weekend box office

A24's documentary "You Can See Everything" took No. 1 at the North American box office in its third weekend with an estimated $10.6 million, narrowly ahead of DC's "Clayface" at $10.4 million, according to Sunday studio estimates.

Sat Oct 31film-tv

A24's Elizabeth Holmes documentary edges 'Clayface' at Friday box office

A24's documentary "You Can See Everything" took in $3.56 million in North America on Friday, narrowly ahead of Warner Bros. and DC's "Clayface" at $3.3 million.

Fri Oct 30courts

Appeals court reinstates jury's antitrust verdict against the NFL in 'Sunday Ticket' case, orders new damages trial

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday reinstated a jury's finding that the NFL violated antitrust law in how it sold its out-of-market "Sunday Ticket" package, and affirmed that a new trial must be held to decide damages, Deadline and Yahoo Sports reported.

Fri Oct 30film-tv

SAG-AFTRA members ratify TV animation contracts with 12.6% raises and AI protections

SAG-AFTRA members voted 94.95% to 5.05% to ratify new television animation and basic cable animation agreements with the studios' bargaining group, the AMPTP, the union said after voting closed Thursday, according to Deadline and Animation World Network.

Fri Oct 30entertainment

Activision to cut real Itaewon crowd-crush footage from 'Call of Duty' after outcry in South Korea

Activision apologized and said it will remove real news footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush in Seoul from the opening cinematic of "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4" in an update on Nov. 12, after objections from victims' families, the BBC and Korea Herald reported.

Thu Oct 29music

Universal Music Group's third-quarter revenue rises 12.3% as subscription growth speeds up

Universal Music Group said Thursday its third-quarter revenue rose 12.3% from a year earlier to €3.394 billion, helped by its acquisition of Downtown Music and faster growth in subscription streaming.

Thu Oct 29business

People Inc. lays off 195 employees, about 6% of staff, mostly in print and legacy web

People Inc., the publisher of People, Entertainment Weekly and other brands, is laying off 195 employees, about 6% of its workforce, CEO Neil Vogel said in a staff memo Thursday, according to Variety, Adweek and TheWrap.

Thu Oct 29film-tv

Netflix develops live-action 'PUBG' series with Donald Glover directing and starring

Netflix is developing a live-action series based on Krafton's battle royale video game PUBG, with Donald Glover set to direct, star, write and executive produce, Krafton announced and Deadline and Variety reported Thursday.

Wed Oct 28film-tv

Iran court sentences filmmaker Jafar Panahi to five more years in prison, his lawyer says

A Tehran Revolutionary Court has sentenced Palme d'Or-winning Iranian director Jafar Panahi in absentia to five years and one month in prison and ordered his assets confiscated, his lawyer Mostafa Nili told the Iranian reformist outlet Emtedad, according to Variety and AP.

Wed Oct 28business

Amazon MGM Studios says it will double investment in original Japanese films and series

Buddy Marini, the new head of Amazon MGM Studios Japan, said Wednesday at the TIFFCOM content market in Tokyo that the company will double its investment in original Japanese content, including live-action films, series and anime, Deadline and Screen International reported.

Wed Oct 28film-tv

Former Lucasfilm chief Kathleen Kennedy named head of LA28 Olympic ceremonies

LA28 on Wednesday named film producer Kathleen Kennedy head of ceremonies and content for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games, putting her in charge of all four opening and closing ceremonies.

Wed Oct 28film-tv

Ken Burns wins inaugural $250,000 Rubenstein Prize for American history

Documentary filmmaker Ken Burns is the first winner of the David M. Rubenstein Prize for the Advancement of American History, a $250,000 award from The New York Historical, the museum and library announced.

Tue Oct 27business

Channel 4 to launch inside Disney+ in the UK and Ireland in early 2027

Channel 4 and The Walt Disney Company announced Tuesday that the British public broadcaster's main TV channel, an on-demand catalog and several new shows released the same day as on Channel 4 will be available on Disney+ in the UK and Ireland from early 2027, at no extra cost to subscribers.

Tue Oct 27music

Neil Young files $10 million copyright suit over Trump rallies' use of 'Rockin' in the Free World'

Neil Young sued the Trump 47 Committee in federal court in Virginia on Monday, seeking $10 million in damages and an order to stop the political committee from playing his song "Rockin' in the Free World" at rallies, according to the complaint as reported by Variety and NBC News.
